title: Projective Hilbert--Mumford criterion for arbitrary SL representations
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq2$, let $E$ be an $r$-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $G=\operatorname{SL}(E)$ be the group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] whose $R$-points are the determinant-one $R$-linear automorphisms of $E\otimes_kR$. Let $V
e0$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with a rational $G$-representation, meaning a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $G	o\operatorname{GL}(V)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(V)(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(V\otimes_kR)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Let $Y$ be a projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective] equipped with a $G$-action and a $G$-equivariant closed immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ parametrizes one-dimensional subspaces of $V$, and $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$ is the dual of its tautological line, with the induced $G$-linearization. Define $Y^{ss}(L)$ by nonvanishing of $G$-invariant global sections of positive tensor powers of $L$. A point $y\in Y(k)$ is stable when it belongs to $Y^{ss}(L)$, its orbit is closed there, and its scheme-theoretic stabilizer has dimension zero. For each nontrivial homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_m	o G$, decompose a nonzero vector $v$ spanning $j(y)$ as $v=\sum_a v_a$ using the integer weight spaces of the restricted representation [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis], and put $
u_\lambda(y)=\min\{a\in\mathbf Z:v_a
e0\}$. Then $y$ is stable if and only if $
u_\lambda(y)<0$ for every such $\lambda$. This assertion holds in every characteristic and permits nonreduced $Y$ and nonreduced zero-dimensional stabilizers.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $E$ and a lift $0\ne v\in V$ of $j(y)$. By [def-sc-general-linear-group], $G=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{ij}]/(\det-1)$ is affine of finite type; affine vector space is affine of finite type, so the orbit map $\alpha_v$ is a morphism between affine finite-type $k$-schemes. By [lem-sfb-projective-stability-affine-orbit-proper], stability of $y$ is exactly properness of $\alpha_v$. We will test the latter by [lem-sfb-affine-properness-formal-arc-test] with $A=k[[t]]$ and $K=k((t))$. These hypotheses require neither a reduced $Y$ nor a smooth stabilizer.

proof.text: The elementary series facts justify using Smith form below. A series with nonzero constant term has an inverse, obtained recursively by solving each coefficient of the product. Every nonzero series is uniquely $t^n u$ for $n\geq0$ and a unit $u$. In a nonzero ideal take the least occurring $n$; its element generates the ideal, since it divides every series of order at least $n$. Thus $A$ is a local principal ideal domain with maximal ideal $(t)\ne0$, hence a DVR by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; its fraction field is $K$. These arguments use the coefficient and product convention of [def-weil-formal-power-series].

proof.text: For $g\in\operatorname{SL}_r(K)$ multiply by $t^N$ to make all entries integral, and apply [lem-sfb-dvr-matrix-smith-powers] to $t^Ng$. Its rank is $r$, so, taking inverses of the two change-of-basis matrices, this yields $g=P D Q$, where $P,Q\in\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$ and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t^{n_1},\ldots,t^{n_r})$ with integers $n_i$. Taking determinants and orders gives $\sum_i n_i=0$ and $\det P\det Q=1$. Put $u=\det P$, $C=\operatorname{diag}(u^{-1},1,\ldots,1)$, $P'=PC$, $Q'=C^{-1}Q$. Since $C$ commutes with $D$, $g=P'DQ'$ and both $P',Q'$ have determinant one. If $g\notin\operatorname{SL}_r(A)$, not all $n_i$ are zero, since otherwise $g=P'Q'$ is integral.

proof.text: Suppose the strict weight inequalities hold but $\alpha_v$ is not proper. The formal-arc test gives $g\in G(K)$ such that $gv\in V\otimes_kA$ but $g$ has no extension in $G(A)$. Use Step 3 and put $w(t)=Q'(t)v$. The given representation is a morphism of group schemes, so $P'^{\pm1}$ and $Q'^{\pm1}$ act by invertible $A$-linear maps. Thus $Dw(t)=P'^{-1}gv$ is integral, and $w(0)=Q'(0)v\ne0$. Let $\delta(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z^{n_i})$; the zero sum makes this a cocharacter of $G$, nontrivial by Step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to $\delta$ and write $w(t)=\sum_a w_a(t)$. Integrality of $Dw(t)$ says $t^a w_a(t)$ is integral for every $a$. For $a<0$, each coordinate of $w_a(t)$ is divisible by $t^{-a}$, so $w_a(0)=0$. With $q=Q'(0)\in G(k)$ and $\lambda=q^{-1}\delta q$, the nonzero weights of $v$ for $\lambda$ are exactly those of $qv=w(0)$ for $\delta$, all nonnegative. This gives $\nu_\lambda(y)\geq0$, a contradiction. Therefore $\alpha_v$ is proper and $y$ stable by Step 1.

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $y$ is stable. By Step 1 the orbit map is proper. If a nontrivial $\lambda:\mathbf G_m	o G$ had $
u_\lambda(y)\geq0$, [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] would give $\lambda(t)v=\sum_a t^a v_a\in V\otimes_kA$, since every occurring $a$ is nonnegative. The formal-arc test would extend $\lambda(t)\in G(K)$ to $G(A)$. This is impossible: apply that same weight-basis theorem to the defining representation on $E$. Its weights $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ sum to zero because $\det\lambda=1$. Nontriviality implies some $b_i
e0$ (if all vanished the group-scheme homomorphism would be the identity cocharacter), and hence some $b_i<0$. In this constant basis the corresponding diagonal entry $t^{b_i}$ is not integral. An $A$-point of $\operatorname{SL}(E)$ has all entries integral, a contradiction. Thus $
u_\lambda(y)<0$ for every nontrivial $\lambda$. All arguments are valid in arbitrary characteristic; they never replace a stabilizer by its tangent space or demand reducedness.
